title: On-Command Grid Bloom
blurb: A skewed white grid blooms out of a lime light haze behind a bold heading, with a flowing gradient CTA whose conic border ring spins.
technique:
This is a faithful rebuild of the background behind Meshy's **"3D, On Command"** call-to-action band. The real effect is **not** a 3D perspective grid or dust motes (that was the earlier wrong guess) — it is a static CSS/SVG light composition built from React component `tf`/`tv` in build chunk `11wz9_xx-0j_m.js`, with colors from stylesheet `14ac6qycc6c_g.css`.

The grid is an SVG `<pattern>` of `40×40` cells whose single L-shaped path `M.5 40V.5H40` draws the left and top edge of each cell, rendered in `white/5` with `mix-blend-mode: overlay`. The whole grid sheet is `skewY(-18deg)` and is fade-masked top-to-bottom with `linear-gradient(#fff, transparent)`. On top of the pattern sit **11 hand-placed "lit" cells** at the exact captured coordinates `[[14,4],[12,5],[16,6],[20,8],[22,9],[24,7],[3,3],[2,1],[7,3],[10,6],[12,2]]` (each a `41×41` rect at `col*40, row*40`, offset `-12,4` to align with the pattern origin).

The lime glow is a `linear-gradient(to right, #e1f9a7/30, #c5f955/30)` wash masked by `radial-gradient(farthest-side at top, white, transparent)` so it blooms from the top-center, plus a large blurred white blob (`blur(26px)`) as a soft volumetric core. The whole light group is clipped by an outer `radial-gradient(800px 400px at top, white 20%, transparent)` mask. On the live site the group renders at `opacity: 0.15`; here it is lifted to `0.5` so the grid and bloom read in a standalone thumbnail — all colors, geometry, masks and relative layer opacities are otherwise kept exactly as captured.

The only motion in the real section belongs to the **CTA button**, reproduced verbatim: a `linear-gradient(155.056deg, #AAFFCA, #BAFF4A, #AAFFCA)` at `200% 200%` size that flows via the `cta-flow` keyframes (`background-position 0 0 → 100% 100%`, `5s ease-in-out`), and a `conic-gradient` border ring — masked with `mask-composite: exclude` to just a `2px` rim — that spins through a CSS `@property --cta-border-angle` over `7s linear`. The accent green is Meshy's real token `--color-accent-base: #c5f955` on a near-black `#0e0e0e` background. No CDN, fonts, or images — fully self-contained.
